This will not be significantly increased or decreased as the result of the project. Both Front Street and Second Street (see Part II, paragraph 5.a) form a major arterial route through the City. The proposed "River Relief Road", part of the logical highway network system, will divert a major share of this traffic away from the project area when it is completed. The minor changes in traffic flow along Front and Second Streets, will not deviate to any measurable degree over levels that would be present, given the absence of the proposed project.
Minor negative effects on atmospheric condition may occur during the short term period of project execution. These will come from demolition of older structures, construction of new buildings, street work, and property rehabilitation. A minor amount of dust and pollutants placed into the atmosphere by this activity cannot be avoided; however, certain measures required by local law, e.g., watering down buildings when they are being demolished and pollution control devices on construction equipment, will greatly reduce this possibility.
On the other hand, once constructed, rehabilitated, or made to comply with local code requirements, structures in the area will have a minor positive impact on the atmosphere from the effect of modernized or repaired heating equipment. This newer equipment operates at a higher combustion efficiency than does older or illegally operating heating equipment. It is anticipated that many of the properties will be converted to cleaner methods of heating i.e., natural gas or electricity, as a result of the proposed rehabilitation program.
The demolition activities will also generate increased amounts of solid waste that must burn in the City's incinerator. The additional pollutants placed into the atmosphere as a result of this cannot be avoided as the increased efficiency capacity of the new incinerator will help to prevent this from being a matter of major concern.
The additional trees in the project area will help to clean the air and lower carbon dioxide levels during the periods of foliage -- a nominal positive impact.
It is not known if the additional power requirements of the project lighting will have any measurable effect on the atmosphere. The additional lights will require approximately 70 kilowatts per day. The amount of pollutants placed into the atmosphere, as a result of producing this much electrical energy (70KW per day), will be nominal.
